app/package.json:8 — 'start': 'node .output/server/index.mjs' serves Nitro's build output, so every request goes through beta-stage software
app/vite.config.ts:6 — plugins: [solidStart(), nitro()] — Nitro participates in every build
app/src/lib/queries.ts:1-37 — data layer uses only stable query/'use server'/createAsync APIs
app/src/app.tsx:2-3 — Router/FileRoutes, stable; app/src/routes/index.tsx:11-19 — documented route preload pattern
app/package.json:12-13 — router 1.0.0 and start 2.1.0: stable but brand-new majors (2026-07-28 / 2026-10-22)
reach.rationale: Exactly one pre-release dependency, but it sits in the most central place possible (the production server engine), alongside a stack of very recently stabilized majors (SolidStart 2.1, Router 1.0, Vite 8). All application code is long-stable API surface.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:6 — Nitro appears in exactly one config line, the documented solidStart()+nitro() pairing
app/package.json:14 — plus one dependency line and the start script; nothing else references nitro
app/src/lib/queries.ts:1-37 — server code is plain 'use server' functions; a deployment-plugin swap would not touch src/
grep over app/src — no unstable_*/experimental_ identifiers or config flags anywhere in app code
containment.rationale: The pre-release surface is fully contained in two lines of config plus package.json; the entire src/ tree would survive swapping the server engine unchanged.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:6 — nitro() is the only documented way to deploy SolidStart v2 to a self-hosted Node server (docs.solidjs.com deployment-plugins guide prescribes this exact plugin pair); there is no stable alternative
app/src/entry-server.tsx:25 — { mode: 'async' } is a documented stable HandlerOptions, chosen so first paint is complete and spec-required fragment links (#moves) resolve on first load
app/src/entry-server.tsx:4-5 — comment states the reason for the async rendering mode
absence — the app does not reach for the newest 2.1 features (ssr: 'data-only', earlyHints), showing it takes only what the spec needs
justification.rationale: The single pre-release dependency is mandated by the stable framework itself, and each non-default choice (async SSR mode) maps to a spec requirement. Nothing is used for novelty.

findings.issue: Nitro is pinned to ^3.0.260903-beta while the v3 line has since moved to release-candidate (3.0.261029-rc, 2026-10-29); npm start runs the app on beta-stage server software, and a caret range on a beta tag will not pick up the RC or the eventual stable
findings.suggestion: Track the RC/stable nitro v3 line (bump to the 261029-rc or later, or 'latest' once v3 ships) and rely on the committed lockfile for reproducibility; re-test build/start after each nitro major bump since v3 explicitly ships breaking changes between beta and RC

findings.issue: The nitro beta drags in an otherwise pre-release transitive stack (h3 ^2.0.1-rc, unstorage 2.0.0-alpha, unenv 2.0.0-rc), so the whole server runtime is pre-release end to end
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change in app code — keep package-lock.json committed (it is) and audit on nitro upgrades

findings.issue: @solidjs/router 1.0.0 (2026-07-28) and @solidjs/start 2.1.0 (2026-10-22) are days-to-months-old stable majors; router 1.0 is explicitly a version realignment of the long-stable 0.16 line, so risk is low but upgrade cadence is brisk
findings.suggestion: Fine as is; note the ecosystem's fast major cadence (SolidStart v2 requires Node 24, which engines already enforces at app/package.json:20-22)

summary: The app is built squarely on the framework's current stable line — SolidStart 2.1, Router 1.0, Vite 8, Solid 1.9 — using only documented APIs and deliberately skipping the shiniest new features. Its single pre-release piece is nitro v3 (beta pin, RC now out), which is nevertheless the officially prescribed deployment plugin for SolidStart v2 and is confined to one config line and two package.json entries. Experimental exposure is real but justified, contained, and easy to swap when Nitro v3 stabilizes.
